statement: Express $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta$ in the form $R\sin(\theta+\alpha)$ with $R>0$, and state its maximum value.
solution: $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta=R\sin(\theta+\alpha)=R\sin\theta\cos\alpha+R\cos\theta\sin\alpha$. Matching coefficients: $R\cos\alpha=3$, $R\sin\alpha=4$, so $R=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$ and $\tan\alpha=4/3$. The maximum value is $R=5$.
hints: Expand $R\sin(\theta+\alpha)$ and match coefficients of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$.
